blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 2

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14-26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 below.

Walking and shoes in eighteenth-century London

A look at changing fashions in footwear and leisure.

A It was difficult to get about in eighteenth-century London. During the first half of that century, the physical mobility of the upper classes in the city had been considerably restricted: the poor condition of the streets did not allow 'walking for pleasure' outside private parks or pleasure gardens. Streets were dirty, rubbish was everywhere and the British climate did not help. Walking could be a risky business. The terrible state of roads, always flooded and muddy, created a metropolitan world of shoe cleaners and street sweepers.

B References to walking are not abundant in early eighteenth-century texts. This is truer for urban spaces than for places in the countryside, where country life had always been dominated by a lifestyle of outdoor activities. For instance, in eighteenth-century London, a sightseer's experience was restricted to touristic places and involved journeys by a series of boats and coaches. Walking was considered to be an activity for the poorer members of society - or simply those who could not afford a coach.

C This situation underwent a sudden improvement in the mid-eighteenth century, with measures implementing the provision of public spaces in which to walk. The first legislation concerning paving in London was passed in 1762, and during the following decades similar laws were enacted in many cities. By the end of the century, areas for walking were commonplace, and far more people were enjoying the pastime than before. Sophie von La Roche writes about metropolitan street life in the diary of her visit to London of 1786. She comments on how many more pedestrians there were on the broad, clean pavements, alongside the houses where, she says, 'many thousands of neatly clad people, eminent men and dressy women, pursue their way safe from the carriages, horses and dirt'. Although the pastime of walking was pursued only in specific spaces designed for the purpose, the number of these spaces increased as the nineteenth century approached. Travelling on foot became smoother and less dangerous.

D Attitudes toward walking through public spaces and their changes over time were visible in the practical designs of fashionable footwear. Protective overshoes and other devices designed to keep feet above the dirty and wet ground soon disappeared, and ease of mobility increased. In the early eighteenth century, the look of men's and women's shoes started to diverge in appearance as a distinction between male and female footwear filtered into production. Contemporary descriptions of the boot and shoe trade underlined the differences between ladies' shoemakers and men's shoemakers too.

E The production of men's and women's footwear required different skills, as the products were essentially different. Men wore more sober footwear, not unlike modern shoes. Their shoes were entirely made of leather, which provided resistance to rain, mud and bad weather. Women's shoes had uppers made of textiles - silk, satin or cloth - and their resistance to bad weather and dirty streets was limited. Only the lower ranks of women wore leather shoes of a form similar to men's. The high-quality shoes for women were often embroidered and were normally worn with protective overshoes, as they were prone to being damaged or disfigured by the conditions of the time.

F The shoes of men and women related to their more general clothing in different ways. Wealthy women's footwear harmonised with their other garments, a harmony that could be effected through matching textiles, general colour, embroidered detail or buckles. In the eighteenth century, men's shoes matched their clothing in different ways, for example with glossy black, red or pink heels. The shoe of an upper-class man also acted as a type of sign which emphasised the difference between the wearer and young boys and women. The shoe also distinguished him from working men who wore leather or cloth protective leggings, ragged shoes and clogs. The symbolic marking of the entry of a wealthy young man into manhood through his shoes, as well as his other dress, may have been of more importance than has previously been acknowledged in costume history.

questionGroups.bodyHtml:
Questions 14-20

Reading Passage 2 has six paragraphs, A-F.

Which paragraph contains the following information?

Write the correct letter, A-F, in boxes 14-20 on your answer sheet. You may use any letter more than once.

ABCDEF
14 details of a legal change affecting conditions in urban areas
15 a reference to how the significance of men's shoes has been overlooked by experts
16 a reference to how gender began to affect shoe design
17 a description of potential problems faced in urban areas
18 a mention of the tough qualities of men's shoes
19 a reference to modes of transport used by visitors to London
20 a mention of the limited areas in early eighteenth-century London where local people could enjoy walking

Questions 21 and 22

Choose TWO letters, A-E.

The writer refers to the relationship between shoes and other clothing. Which TWO of the following are mentioned?

Questions 23-26

Complete the summary below.

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

Walking in the eighteenth century

Only a few texts dating from the first few decades of the eighteenth century actually make reference to walking. In fact, in London, only people who were less well-off had to walk rather than take a 23 . The situation, though, was different in the 24 .

Things changed mid-century, as more public spaces for walking were made available in London, and a number of English cities were affected by similar governmental decisions during the second half of the century. As a consequence, according to Sophie von La Roche, the number of 25 rose dramatically, because many people were able to walk on wide 26 away from the traffic.

items.text:
（1）题目 14：details of a legal change affecting conditions in urban areas
题目翻译：影响城市环境状况的一项法律变化的细节。
答案：C
定位：正文 C 段，第2句
原文：The first legislation concerning paving in London was passed in 1762, and during the following decades similar laws were enacted in many cities.
译文：第一部关于伦敦铺路的法律于1762年通过；之后几十年，许多城市也颁布了类似法律。

解析：题干 legal change 对应 legislation 和 similar laws，urban areas 对应 London 与 many cities；法律内容是改善铺路条件，因此定位C段。

（2）题目 15：a reference to how the significance of men’s shoes has been overlooked by experts
题目翻译：提到专家过去忽视了男鞋的重要意义。
答案：F
定位：正文 F 段，末句
原文：may have been of more importance than has previously been acknowledged in costume history
译文：其重要性可能超过服装史研究过去所承认的程度。

解析：significance 对应 importance，has been overlooked by experts 对应 previously been acknowledged in costume history：服装史研究低估了富裕青年男鞋所具有的成年象征意义。

（3）题目 16：a reference to how gender began to affect shoe design
题目翻译：提到性别如何开始影响鞋子的设计。
答案：D
定位：正文 D 段，第3句
原文：the look of men’s and women’s shoes started to diverge in appearance as a distinction between male and female footwear filtered into production
译文：随着男女鞋的区别逐渐进入生产环节，男鞋和女鞋的外观开始分化。

解析：gender 对应 male and female，began to affect 对应 started to diverge 与 filtered into production，完整描述了性别差异开始影响鞋类设计。

（4）题目 17：a description of potential problems faced in urban areas
题目翻译：描述城市环境中可能遇到的问题。
答案：A
定位：正文 A 段，中后部
原文：Streets were dirty, rubbish was everywhere and the British climate did not help. Walking could be a risky business. The terrible state of roads, always flooded and muddy
译文：街道肮脏、垃圾遍地，英国气候也没有帮助；步行可能很危险，道路常常积水且泥泞不堪。

解析：A段连续列出城市步行会遇到的脏乱、垃圾、天气、积水、泥泞和风险，完整对应 potential problems faced in urban areas。

（5）题目 18：a mention of the tough qualities of men’s shoes
题目翻译：提到男鞋耐用、结实的特性。
答案：E
定位：正文 E 段，第3句
原文：Their shoes were entirely made of leather, which provided resistance to rain, mud and bad weather.
译文：男鞋完全由皮革制成，能够抵御雨水、泥泞和恶劣天气。

解析：tough qualities 由皮革材质及其 resistance to rain, mud and bad weather 具体体现，因此定位E段。

（6）题目 19：a reference to modes of transport used by visitors to London
题目翻译：提到伦敦游客使用的交通方式。
答案：B
定位：正文 B 段，第3句
原文：a sightseer’s experience was restricted to touristic places and involved journeys by a series of boats and coaches
译文：观光客的活动限于旅游地点，行程包括乘坐一系列船只和马车。

解析：visitors 对应 sightseer，modes of transport 对应 boats and coaches，因此答案为B段。

（7）题目 20：a mention of the limited areas in early eighteenth-century London where local people could enjoy walking
题目翻译：提到18世纪早期伦敦本地人能够享受步行的有限区域。
答案：A
定位：正文 A 段，第2句
原文：the poor condition of the streets did not allow ‘walking for pleasure’ outside private parks or pleasure gardens
译文：街道状况很差，人们只能在私人公园或游乐花园内进行休闲散步。

解析：limited areas 对应 outside private parks or pleasure gardens 不允许休闲散步，反向说明当时可享受步行的范围仅限这些场所，因此仍定位A段。

items.text:
（1）题目 21：（题干见题目区）
题目翻译：关于鞋与其他服装之间的关系，作者提到了以下哪两项？
答案：A（Shoes for rich women were designed to match their dress in various ways.）
定位：正文 F 段，第1至2句
原文：Wealthy women's footwear harmonised with their other garments, a harmony that could be effected through matching textiles, general colour, embroidered detail or buckles.
译文：富裕女性的鞋履与其他服装相协调，这种协调可以通过匹配面料、整体颜色、刺绣细节或鞋扣来实现。

解析：rich women 对应 wealthy women，match their dress 对应 harmonised with their other garments；原文列出的面料、颜色、刺绣和鞋扣正是 various ways，因此 A 正确。

（2）题目 22：（题干见题目区）
题目翻译：关于鞋与其他服装之间的关系，作者提到了以下哪两项？
答案：D（Wealthy men's shoes set the wearer apart from other groups.）
定位：正文 F 段，第4至5句
原文：The shoe of an upper-class man also acted as a type of sign which emphasised the difference between the wearer and young boys and women. The shoe also distinguished him from working men.
译文：上层男性的鞋也是一种身份标志，强调穿着者与年轻男孩及女性的区别，也把他与劳动男性区分开来。

解析：wealthy men 对应 upper-class man，set the wearer apart from other groups 对应 emphasised the difference 和 distinguished him from working men，因此 D 正确。

items.text:
（1）题目 23：Only a few texts dating from the first few decades of the eighteenth century actually make reference to walking. In fact, in London, only people who were less well-off had to walk rather than take a ________. The situation, though, was different in the ________.
题目翻译：在伦敦，较贫困的人只能步行，而不能乘坐______。
答案：coach
定位：正文 B 段，末句
原文：Walking was considered to be an activity for the poorer members of society — or simply those who could not afford a coach.
译文：步行被认为是社会中较贫困人群的活动，或者简单说，是那些乘不起马车的人所做的事。

解析：less well-off 对应 poorer members of society，had to walk rather than take 对应 could not afford；冠词 a 后应填原文单数 coach。

（2）题目 24：Only a few texts dating from the first few decades of the eighteenth century actually make reference to walking. In fact, in London, only people who were less well-off had to walk rather than take a ________. The situation, though, was different in the ________.
题目翻译：不过，______的情况不同。
答案：countryside
定位：正文 B 段，第2句
原文：This is truer for urban spaces than for places in the countryside, where country life had always been dominated by a lifestyle of outdoor activities.
译文：这种情况在城市空间比乡村地区更明显；乡村生活一直以户外活动为主。

解析：题干 The situation was different in the... 对应原文城市与 places in the countryside 的直接对比，因此答案是 countryside。

（3）题目 25：Things changed mid-century, as more public spaces for walking were made available in London, and a number of English cities were affected by similar governmental decisions during the second half of the century. As a consequence, according to Sophie von La Roche, the number of ________ rose dramatically, because many people were able to walk on wide ________ away from the traffic.
题目翻译：据 Sophie von La Roche 记载，______的数量大幅增加。
答案：pedestrians
定位：正文 C 段，第5句
原文：She comments on how many more pedestrians there were on the broad, clean pavements
译文：她谈到宽阔、干净的人行道上出现了多得多的行人。

解析：according to Sophie von La Roche 锁定她的评论，the number ... rose 对应 how many more；被计数的对象是 pedestrians。

（4）题目 26：Things changed mid-century, as more public spaces for walking were made available in London, and a number of English cities were affected by similar governmental decisions during the second half of the century. As a consequence, according to Sophie von La Roche, the number of ________ rose dramatically, because many people were able to walk on wide ________ away from the traffic.
题目翻译：许多人可以在远离车流的宽阔______上步行。
答案：pavements
定位：正文 C 段，第5句
原文：on the broad, clean pavements, alongside the houses where, she says ‘many thousands of neatly clad people, eminent men and dressy women, pursue their way safe from the carriages, horses and dirt’
译文：在房屋旁宽阔、干净的人行道上，成千上万衣着整洁的人可以安全行走，避开马车、马匹和污物。

解析：wide 对应 broad，away from the traffic 对应 safe from the carriages and horses；具体步行位置是 pavements。
